name: Rachel Kim-Hoffman

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal-plan subscription. Video hero, generic tagline.
five_sec.who_for: Mainstream families who want recipes picked.
five_sec.trust_why: Feels like an established brand, but the design is dated and the hero communicates nothing except 'stress bad'.
five_sec.next_step: Skip the video, scroll for pricing and Instacart.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: How-it-works illustration is a phone with a checklist; step 2 sends a list to grocers.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Email-capture pop-up on load, no visible price, and the sample recipes skew adult (rosemary-mustard pork chops, bok choy). My 3-year-old eats none of that.
full_page.whats_missing: Price on the page, product screenshots, how many nights the plan covers.

EM.quote: Instacart logo, Kid Friendly plan, then a collapsed accordion for price. That's friction by design.

five_sec.what_is_it: Recipe organizer, planner and grocery list.
five_sec.trust_why: Ratings on both stores up top, no card required.
five_sec.next_step: Check whether it plans for me. It doesn't look like it.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Tagline: recipes, meal plans and grocery lists in one app.

full_page.what_stopped_me: It's a tool for doing the work, and the work is what I'm paying to outsource.

PTE.quote: 'You're in control. Add your recipes, move meals around anytime.' That's the opposite of my brief.

five_sec.what_is_it: AI that decides dinner for the family.
five_sec.who_for: Overloaded parents who want the decision gone. Me.
five_sec.trust_why: Polished app mockup, 90,000+ families, press logos further down. Looks like a funded product, not a side project. The CEO-letter CTA is odd though.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Menu app screens with 'Replace' and 'Modify' on each dinner.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Pricing is message-metered and the meal page says 'prices are available when you download the app' while the pricing page says $25/month. Inconsistent. Also 'AI writes a recipe just for you' makes me wonder about quality.
full_page.whats_missing: A clear plan price for meals only; kid-specific handling.

OL.quote: 'Ollie takes over the decision itself.' Yes. That's the job. I'd pay for it, I just want one price, not message top-ups.

five_sec.what_is_it: Dinner planner: family votes by text, list goes into your Instacart or Walmart cart.
five_sec.who_for: Families with kids old enough to text.
five_sec.trust_why: Clean enough, Instacart badge helps, explicit 'we don't deliver food'. But it's a wall of text with no product screenshot on the first screen.
five_sec.next_step: Check the Instacart flow and pricing.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Bold line: 'We don't deliver food. We plan your week and send your grocery list.'

full_page.what_stopped_me: The headline feature is a vote by text; my kids are 7 and 3, so the hero pitch isn't for me. 'Over 500 families' and a store-price chart of upstate New York stores reads like a founder's side project. Footer full of 'Shop' and 'Kitchen essentials' links doesn't help.
full_page.whats_missing: Real app screenshots on the home page, and 'we decide the week for you' as the default promise.

DD.quote: Built on the Instacart Developer Platform, five nights, free. Good. But a Wegmans vs. Tops price chart means nothing in Ballard.

five_sec.what_is_it: HelloFresh, with a 'mystery box' offer gate.
five_sec.who_for: New customers they're trying to hook.
five_sec.trust_why: I'm a current customer, so I know the product. The gamified pop-up is cheap.
five_sec.next_step: Close it. I'm here to compare, not to buy more.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Meal-kit boxes; it's literally the product.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Already paying ~$100 a week for 3 dinners after unannounced price creep. Prices hidden behind a zip box.

HF.quote: Still no price without a zip code. Which is how I ended up paying $100 a week without noticing.

dd_offer.why: Pricing card states it: Family free 14 days, no card, $4.99 or $39 after if you add a card, email 3 days before.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: Texting features lapse, I stay on Free. No charge since I never added a card.

head_to_head.reason: It's the only one that reads as a finished product promising to make the decisions for me; the price is noise next to my HelloFresh bill.

EM.reason: DinnerDrop shows its price and an actual week; eMeals hides both.

PTE.reason: DinnerDrop plans for me; Plan to Eat hands me a toolkit.

OL.reason: Ollie looks like a real, polished product that decides for me; DinnerDrop's hero is a kids' vote and an upstate store chart.

HF.reason: Five nights in my existing Instacart for free versus $400 a month for three.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page first screen: replace the text-heavy voting pitch with real app screenshots and a 'we pick your five dinners' promise (voting as an option), and move the upstate NY store chart off the home page.
